title: Actual reconstruction restricted to uniform finite-Tor bounds
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a prime l different from its characteristic, a finite extension E/Q_l, and a finite-type scheme T over D.k. The actual coefficient reduction/total-limit adjunction restricts to the equivalence in Reconstruction l E T [def-sf-exceptional-integral-reconstruction-interfaces]; in particular Nonempty (Reconstruction l E T). Its comparison isomorphisms, unit, counit, sequence resolutions and shifts are those of that actual adjunction.

proof.text: Transport intrinsic constructibility, common cohomological support and Tor amplitude across each reductionEvaluation isomorphism. Thus the integral finite-Tor predicate is precisely completeness plus LevelBounds of reduction. Isomorphisms preserve homology and its zero objects; the Tor argument transports the input representative isomorphism.

proof.text: Reduction is normalized. On a normalized system actual reconstruction gives completeness of its limit and an invertible counit; evaluate that counit to transport the same intervals to the reductions of the limit. Restrict both functors and the ambient adjunction along their full inclusions. Its unit and counit map to the original ambient maps, so the full inclusions reflect their invertibility. Mathlib Adjunction.toEquivalence now produces the equivalence and exactly the required map equations.

theorem exceptionalIntegralReconstructionEquivalence
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p) (T : Scheme.{u})
    [T.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (T ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (T ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] :
    Nonempty (Reconstruction l E T)
